title: Accountable for the Fire We Start

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a fire breaks out and spreads into thornbushes so that it burns shocks of grain or standing grain or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make restitution." - Exodus 22:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A small fire, lit perhaps for a good reason, spreads beyond control and destroys a neighbour's harvest. God's verdict is clear: the one who started it is responsible, even though the destruction went further than intended. When we set something in motion, we are accountable for where it goes, not only for what we planned.

How true this is of more than literal fires. A careless word can spread like flame through a family or a workplace. A bit of gossip, a sharp comment, a rumour started "just in fun" — these can burn through relationships and reputations long after we have forgotten we lit them. James warns us that the tongue is a small spark that can set a whole forest ablaze (Jas 3:5-6). We are responsible for the fires our words and actions start.

This calls us to a holy carefulness. Before we speak, before we act, it is worth asking: where might this spread? Whose "field" could this burn? And where we have already started a fire, God calls us to own it and help repair the damage rather than walk away. May God make us people who bring warmth without destruction, and who take responsibility for the flames we cannot fully control.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What "fires" have my words or actions started that I need to take responsibility for?
How can I be more careful about where my speech and choices might spread?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard my tongue and my actions from starting fires that harm others. Where I have caused damage, give me the humility to own it and help repair it. Amen.
